headline: 英國衛報藝文評論四則
context: 英國《衛報》今天一次刊出四篇評論：重啟版影集《未宣戰爭》（The Undeclared War）評論說比前作更有張力，但劇情圍繞在地堡打字終究不夠有戲。查理·沃克（Charlie Walker）新書記錄他的西伯利亞徒步之旅，評論形容全書美麗與驚駭交織。皇家莎士比亞劇團的《櫻桃園》被評為卡司星光閃亮，舞台呈現卻少了火花。紀錄片《問問E珍》追蹤專欄作家E·珍·卡蘿（E Jean Carroll）多年來與川普的訴訟拉鋸，評論說她比外界想像的更堅韌。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The rebooted GCHQ digital warfare series has more zip than its predecessor – but people bashing away on computers in a bunker near Cheltenham is inherently unsexy If the espionage battles of the future are going to be fought online, TV thrillers will have to reflect that fact, much as they might not want to. Cyber-attacks, cross-border malware and digital misinformation just aren’t especially televisual: whatever you do, you always end up with a speed-typing nerd muttering “Shit!” as gobbledegook scrolls across a monitor and red lights flash in the distance. In 2022, Channel 4’s missable drama The Undeclared War tried to crack the problem by throwing heavyweight film-making pedigree at it. Peter Kosminsky, the esteemed director behind Wolf Hall and The Government Inspector, had evidently researched the back end out of the subject, presenting the details of an imagined campaign of Russian interference in Britain’s daily digital functionality – and, from there, the democratic process of an election – in a way that real-life sleepless nerds said was credible enough. Continue reading...
sources.title: The Undeclared War review – Simon Pegg’s cyber-attack thriller fails to push any of the right buttons

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Moments of beauty and horror punctuate this account of an ill-timed sub-zero camping trip In late February 2022, Charlie Walker set off on a hiking holiday in northern Siberia. In temperatures as low as -50C, he intended to trek a thousand miles north along the frozen surface of the river Lena, then out across the solid Laptev Sea to the port town of Tiksi, before finally flying home to London. “The plan,” he writes, “was simple in concept.” A sub-zero camping trip through a region populated by wolves and bears and scarred by centuries of historical trauma, in a country that was about to invade one of its neighbours: what could possibly go wrong? On Thin Ice is Walker’s third travelogue. Previous excursions have included a 43,000-mile bicycle ride across three continents, a 1,000-mile solo walk through the Gobi desert, and a river trip down the Congo in a leaky canoe. When not performing incredible feats of forward motion, according to his website, he gives talks to business leaders on subjects such as “risk taking” and “the line between courage and recklessness”. Reading his latest, it’s clear he’s familiar with the terrain on both sides of that line. Continue reading...
sources.title: On Thin Ice by Charlie Walker review – a Siberian adventure goes off the rails

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Swan Theatre, Stratford-Upon-Avon Tamara Harvey’s production of Chekhov’s final play can seem woolly in meaning and soft-edged tone mutes its force Laura Wade’s reworking of Anton Chekhov’s final, plaintive play brings a dazzle of big names. Helen Hunt is the aristocratic matriarch Madame Ranyevskaya, Bill Pullman her brother, and Kenneth Branagh (so soon after his lead role in the Royal Shakespeare’s production of The Tempest) their nemesis, Lopakhin, a shopkeeper’s son here who takes over the reins of the family estate and represents the rising forces against Russia’s old order of ossified elites. But for such a starry cast Tamara Harvey’s production has a disappointing lack of sparkle. You do not feel the story’s charge, its complications around love and its stinging losses. The tone is too soft-edged, almost endearing, and the cast such an ensemble that there is no magnetic centre to hold you. Continue reading...
sources.title: The Cherry Orchard review – RSC’s starry cast brings disappointing lack of sparkle

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Ivy Meeropol’s engrossing film follows former star columnist E Jean Carroll, now in her 80s, battles through an unfinished series of legal disputes Donald Trump has almost succeeded in an insidiously sneaky trick of auto-uncancelling on the #MeToo issue, implying that he is above and beyond and constitutionally exempt, despite being caught on tape boasting of sexual violence. Through a combination of bluster, bad faith, threats, abuse and the simple fact of being US president and flooding the zone on a grander international stage, and moreover with an aggressive army of online trolls at his disposal, he has got away with it. So far. But among his accusers, the one who has so far been successful in two civil suits is the journalist and former advice columnist E Jean Carroll, showing remarkable courage and indomitable good humour. She is the subject of this engrossing documentary from film-maker Ivy Meeropol, co-produced by former Vanity Fair editor Graydon Carter, who incidentally has perhaps a few hail marys of his own to offer for having at first ducked the Jeffrey Epstein story . Carroll had an uproarious career in New York media in the 80s and 90s, in which she was a wisecracking Rosalind Russell-slash-Joan Rivers figure, creating a tough broad persona; she was in fact sometimes less than sympathetic to Paula Jones and Anita Hill in the Bill Clinton and Clarence Thomas cases. Carroll had a TV advice show called Ask E Jean (given to her, as she points out without comment, by the notorious exec Roger Ailes, himself an abuser brought low by #MeToo) . Continue reading...
sources.title: Ask E Jean review – Trump survivor turns out to be tougher than he thought as she fights on

英國衛報藝文評論四則

英國《衛報》今天一次刊出四篇評論。重啟版影集《未宣戰爭》比前作更有張力，但劇情圍繞在地堡裡打字，終究不夠精彩。查理·沃克的新書記錄他的西伯利亞徒步之旅，評論形容全書美麗與驚駭交織。皇家莎士比亞劇團的《櫻桃園》卡司星光閃亮，舞台呈現卻被評缺乏火花。紀錄片《問問E珍》追蹤專欄作家E·珍·卡蘿多年來與川普的訴訟拉鋸，評論說她比外界想像的更堅韌。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 7 月 22 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 今天有四篇藝文評論。重啟版影集《未宣戰爭》，評論說比前作更有張力，但劇情圍繞在地堡裡打字，終究不夠精彩。有一本新書記錄作者在西伯利亞的徒步之旅，評論形容全書美麗與驚駭交織。皇家莎士比亞劇團重新搬演的《櫻桃園》，卡司星光閃亮，舞台呈現卻被評缺了火花。還有一部紀錄片，追蹤一位專欄作家跟川普多年的訴訟拉鋸，評論說她比外界想像的更堅韌。
